items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1971-07-09
items.q: The mention of 'Murray the Cay' appears in the [INTERVIEWER]'s turn as part of a radio intro ('This is Murray the Cay from Monitor 71... Bidding an affectionate farewell to... Louis Armstrong'). The interviewee (Louis Armstrong) does not speak about Murray the Cay, nor does he indicate a personal re

ctx.x: Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. This is Murray the Cay from Monitor 71. Bidding an affectionate farewell to one of the giants of the world of popular music, Louis Armstrong. And what you're hearing is sleepy time down south, something you've always heard when he made a public appearance. Louie always loved appearing in public, even when he wasn't scheduled to and wasn't getting paid for it. Doc Severinsen, another pretty fair trumpet player, remembers such an incident. Well, a couple of years ago when…

¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ Uh, New Orleans, my name was Satchel Mow. So this English editor of the Melody Maker magazine, he shook my hand and said, ¶¶ So I was surprised and I asked the colored trombone player who joined me from Paris. I said, this cat called me Sat Smoll and my name is Sat Ramal. So he told me, he said, a man thinks you have more mouth. That's all. And I'm stuck with it, so that's the way it was.
